# `cfmat.strategies`

<!-- generated by tools/gen_api_docs.py; do not edit -->

Strategies as code and as data (M10, M12).

```text
The package namespace re-exports the classic signal generators from ``signals``
(``from cfmat import strategies; strategies.sma_crossover(...)``).

    signals      vectorised signal functions: crossovers, momentum, mean reversion, pairs
    rules        the Strategy Creator's rule language (safe ``ast`` evaluator)
    spec         ``StrategySpec``: a strategy as data, with JSON round-trip
    templates    library of ready-made ``StrategySpec`` strategies
```

### `cfmat.strategies.rules`

The rule language of the Strategy Creator (M12).

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `available_functions` | `def available_functions() -> list[str]` | Every name the rule language accepts: functions, patterns and price fields. |
| `Evaluator` | `class Evaluator(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> None` | Evaluate rule strings against one set of bars, caching every sub-expression. |
| `Evaluator.boolean` | `boolean(self, expr: str) -> pd.Series` | Evaluate a rule and return a boolean Series (missing values count as False). |
| `register` | `def register(name: str)` | Add a function to the rule language: ``fn(bars, *args) -> Series``. |

### `cfmat.strategies.signals`

Signal generators for the classic strategy families (M10).

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `bollinger_mean_reversion` | `def bollinger_mean_reversion(close: pd.Series, window: int = 20, entry_z: float = 2.0, exit_z: float = 0.5) -> pd.Series` | Fade stretched moves: short above +entry_z, long below −entry_z, flatten once \|z\| falls back under ``exit_z``. |
| `cross_sectional_momentum` | `def cross_sectional_momentum(prices: pd.DataFrame, lookback: int = 126, skip: int = 21, top_n: int = 3) -> pd.DataFrame` | Jegadeesh & Titman style: each day hold the ``top_n`` best performers over ``lookback`` days, skipping the most recent ``skip`` days. Equal weights. |
| `hedge_ratio` | `def hedge_ratio(y: pd.Series, x: pd.Series) -> tuple[float, float]` | OLS of y on x. Returns (beta, alpha). |
| `pairs_signals` | `def pairs_signals(y: pd.Series, x: pd.Series, formation: int = 250, window: int = 30, entry_z: float = 2.0, exit_z: float = 0.5, beta_window: int \| None = None) -> pd.DataFrame` | Statistical-arbitrage pair on the spread y − beta·x. |
| `rolling_hedge_ratio` | `def rolling_hedge_ratio(y: pd.Series, x: pd.Series, window: int = 60) -> pd.Series` | Rolling OLS beta so the pair can be traded without look-ahead. |
| `rsi_reversal` | `def rsi_reversal(close: pd.Series, period: int = 14, low: float = 30, high: float = 70) -> pd.Series` | Long when RSI is oversold, short when overbought, flat in between. |
| `short_term_signal` | `def short_term_signal(close: pd.Series, lookback: int = 1, direction: int = 1) -> pd.Series` | Follow (``direction=+1``, momentum) or fade (``direction=-1``, reversal) the sign of the last ``lookback``-day move. Long/short every day. |
| `sma_crossover` | `def sma_crossover(close: pd.Series, fast: int = 20, slow: int = 50, allow_short: bool = False) -> pd.Series` | Trend following: long when the fast average is above the slow one. |
| `time_series_momentum` | `def time_series_momentum(close: pd.Series, lookback: int = 126, allow_short: bool = True) -> pd.Series` | Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012): trade the sign of the trailing return. |

### `cfmat.strategies.spec`

``StrategySpec``: a strategy as data (rules, exits, parameters), JSON round-trip (M12).

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `StrategySpec` | `class StrategySpec(name: str, long_entry: list[str] = <factory>, long_exit: list[str] = <factory>, short_entry: list[str] = <factory>, short_exit: list[str] = <factory>, stop_atr: float \| str \| None = None, target_atr: float \| str \| None = None, trail_atr: float \| str \| None = None, max_bars: int \| str \| None = None, atr_period: int = 14, params: dict = <factory>, category: str = 'custom', description: str = '') -> None` | A strategy as data: entry and exit rules, protective exits and parameters. |
| `StrategySpec.resolve` | `resolve(self, **overrides) -> StrategySpec` | Fill ``{placeholders}`` from ``params`` updated with ``overrides``. |
| `StrategySpec.to_dict` | `to_dict(self) -> dict` | The spec as a plain dict. |
| `StrategySpec.to_json` | `to_json(self, path: str \| os.PathLike \| None = None) -> str` | The spec as JSON text; also written to ``path`` when given. |
